newsitem.title: USA: Rights group setting up Wall St. office.
newsitem.headline: Rights group setting up Wall St. office.

text.p: Civil rights leader Jesse Jackson announced Tuesday that his Rainbow PUSH Coalition will open a Wall Street office to monitor how corporate America offers opportunities to minorities -- and lead boycotts if necessary.

The Rev. Jackson said the group will conduct research and educate minority consumers on employment opportunities and treatment of minorities at a wide variety of companies, including automakers, food companies, telecommunications companies and mutual funds.

"It's not that we're looking for boycott targets. We're looking for trading partners," Jackson told a news conference following a speech at the Automotive News World Congress, an annual meeting of automotive industry executives.
The Rainbow PUSH Coalition Wall Street Bureau will formally open its doors in New York on Wednesday.

Jackson said the group also planned to announce an agreement with Mitsubishi Motors Corp. that he said will set a good example of how automakers can be less exclusionary regarding blacks and other minorities.

The former Democratic presidential aspirant and other black leaders recently met with Mitsubishi and other Japanese automakers to discuss how they can improve employment opportunties for minorities in the United States.
Jackson said the new Wall Street office will publish a monthly newsletter that rates companies on how many minority executives and board members they have and what kind of opportunities they offer.
The newsletter will be sent to 20,000 customers in each of 50 large markets, meaning it will reach 1 million people who can make decisions on what stocks to buy and where to shop, Jackson said.
"Those businesses who do not trade with us must not expect us to trade with them," he said.
